newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore hikes petrol and diesel pump prices.
newsitem.headline: Singapore hikes petrol and diesel pump prices.

text.p: Singapore petrol and diesel pump prices rose over the weekend, to become one of the highest in Asia, following hikes in wholesale prices, industry sources said on Monday.
"The increase in pump price is a reflection of higher cost as well as higher operating costs," said a statement from Shell, the largest retailer with around 87 stations.
"The higher product cost is reflected by the higher posted prices (ie ex-refinery wholesale prices), compounded by the rising U.S. dollar in recent months," Shell said.
Sources said all six retailers - Shell, Mobil, British Petroleum, Exxon Corp, Singapore Petroleum Co and Caltex, a Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc joint venture - had increased prices over the weekend.
Diesel, last increased on November 2, rose 2.00 cents per litre to S$0.571.
Petrol or gasoline prices were raised 4.00 cents per litre, double the last price rise on February 12 of 2.00 cents.
The latest price rises left unleaded 98-octane at S$1.226 ($0.85) per litre, unleaded 92-octane at S$1.16, and premium leaded at S$1.347.
Since February, international gasoline and diesel prices have risen by $1.50 to $2.00 per barrel.
Petrol pump prices in Japan, capped by a retail price war, are just a shade higher at 106 yen ($0.855) than those in Singapore.
Last year, total gasoline retail sales in Singapore were estimated by traders at around 5.3 million barrels, while diesel sales were estimated at 2.3 million barrels. ($1=S$1.44, 124 yen)
